title: Frittata
subtitle: Italian baked egg dish with roasted vegetables and feta
excerpt: A frittata is Italy's version of an open-faced omelette -- started on the hob and finished in the oven. It works with almost any combination of vegetables, cheese, and herbs. This version uses courgette, red pepper, spinach, and feta, but it is a framework more than a fixed recipe.
sourceNotes: Frittata is a staple of Italian home cooking. The word comes from the Italian verb friggere, to fry. Unlike a French omelette, it is cooked slowly over low heat, often finished under the grill or in the oven.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Frittata is good at room temperature. Make up to 2 hours ahead.

content.text: Use an oven-safe frying pan or cast-iron skillet. If yours has a plastic handle, wrap it in foil before putting it under the grill.
Preheat the oven to 180C. Heat the oil in an oven-safe 26cm frying pan over medium heat. Cook the courgette and red pepper for 5 minutes until softened.
Add the garlic and spinach. Cook for 2 minutes until the spinach has wilted. Season.
Beat the eggs with the parmesan and season. Pour over the vegetables in the pan.
Scatter the feta over the top. Cook on the hob for 3 minutes until the edges are set.
Transfer the pan to the oven. Bake for 10 to 12 minutes until just set in the centre.
Rest for 5 minutes before slicing. Serve warm or at room temperature.

items.fix: The centre should still have a slight wobble when you take it from the oven. It sets as it rests.

items.symptom: Bottom is burnt before the top is set
items.cause: Too much heat on the hob stage
items.fix: Keep hob heat to medium-low for the first stage and rely on the oven to finish.

content.text: The frittata is found all over Italy, with different regional fillings. In the south, it might include pasta or vegetables; in the north, cured meats or cheese. It is the kind of dish made from whatever needs using up. Unlike an omelette, it is never rushed -- the low, slow cook is the whole point.
